methodological_status: same-context, non-blind, not independently read or budget-matched

cases.title: Varnish: social consequence without narrated shame
fixture: Mara publicly cuts off Niko's warning that the varnish on a frame is not dry
Ten minutes later the varnish marks her cuff as she lifts the frame
No apology is required in the source facts
cases.source_profile: Austen/E03-02: narrated physical event can carry character evaluation; do not imitate Austen diction
cases.raw: Mara interrupted Niko's warning and told the staff the frame was dry. Ten minutes later, when she lifted it, varnish marked her cuff. Niko handed her a rag. She accepted it without saying anything.
cases.initial_intention: State the public error and what follows, without inventing a private monologue.

perceived.finding: A public dismissal is established before the physical proof; these lenses track overlapping event relations.
The stain is a physical consequence that also changes how the previous assertion reads.

perceived.witness: She accepted it without saying anything
perceived.finding: Silence could suggest embarrassment, annoyance or mere attention; it does not prove remorse.

cases.intervention: Make the original dismissal an audible act and leave the social aftermath in gesture; no explicit psychological interpretation.
cases.variant: “Dry,” Mara said, cutting Niko off in front of the staff. Ten minutes later she lifted the frame and got varnish on her cuff. Niko held out a rag. She took it.
cases.change_scope: local direct speech and gesture instead of explaining dismissal or silence
cases.criticism: The raw version may be smoother; 'got varnish' is unremarkable and 'she took it' is not guaranteed to carry more emotion. The revision makes dialogue more explicit but does not prove literary gain.

cases.title: Painting: physical reclassification with no cosmic flourish
fixture: A museum guard sees a white line crossing a painting
He initially thinks it is glare from gallery lighting
He moves sideways but the line persists
At close range a tear in the canvas exposes the white wall behind
No vandal identity or cause is established
cases.source_profile: Giono/R10: a material observation can be reclassified by later physical disclosure; do not borrow cosmic diction or violence
cases.raw: The guard thought the white line across the painting was a reflection from the gallery lights. He moved sideways, but the line stayed where it was. He went closer and found a tear in the canvas; the white wall showed through.
cases.initial_intention: Show a false identification revised by observation, without inventing a perpetrator.

perceived.finding: One visible mark is available for two competing physical explanations.
A movement supplies evidence rather than mere atmospheric business.
A close view resolves line as exposed wall rather than glare.

cases.intervention: Trust the physical step and final evidence; remove explanatory framing without changing the cause.
cases.variant: The guard stepped left to lose the glare. The white line across the painting didn't move. Up close, he could see the wall through a tear in the canvas.
cases.change_scope: compress explanation and delay explicit physical reclassification until final clause
cases.criticism: 'To lose the glare' may sound like evading brightness rather than testing an optical hypothesis. The raw version is more precise about his initial assumption; shorter does not establish better.

cases.title: Recycling notice: refusal to stylize
cases.genre: public-information notice; all facts are invented exercise fixtures
fixture: Existing council collection service accepts large appliances
cases.source_profile: none; source style tools not recruited
cases.raw: The council will open a recycling drop-off point on 1 November. It will accept household batteries and small electronics, but not large appliances; residents can use the existing collection service for those.
cases.initial_intention: Deliver correct service information directly and efficiently.

perceived.finding: Date establishes when the new service becomes available.

perceived.witness: batteries and small electronics, but not large appliances
perceived.finding: One clause provides positive eligibility and a negative boundary.
Gives an alternative action for excluded objects.

cases.criticism: Could be broken into shorter sentences for accessibility in some channels, but there is no identified need in the fixture; no claimed reader evidence.
